app.name: Dropbox
app.description: A cloud storage and file synchronization service that lets you store, share, and access your files from anywhere.

verdict.one_liner: Dropbox does not sell your data to advertisers and gives you solid controls to access, download, and delete your files and account.
verdict.summary: Dropbox collects account information, stored files, contacts, usage activity, and device identifiers. The company explicitly states it will not sell data to advertisers. It shares information with trusted third parties for support, corporate affiliates, and collaborators. Third-party apps connected via APIs exchange data under their own terms. Users can access, amend, download, and delete personal data through account settings. After account deletion, Dropbox initiates deletion after 30 days, though residual copies may persist on backups or longer where legal obligations demand.
verdict.recommendation_reason: Dropbox has strong privacy practices with no ad tracking, no data selling, and good user controls for data deletion and export.

red.title: Shares data with third parties
red.plain_english: Dropbox shares your data with trusted third-party companies that help run the service, like customer support providers.

red.title: Collects device identifiers
red.plain_english: Dropbox collects device identifiers to recognize your devices and maintain security.

green.title: No ads or ad tracking
green.plain_english: Dropbox does not sell your data to advertisers and does not use your data to show you targeted ads.

green.title: Strong user data controls
green.plain_english: You can access, amend, download, and delete your personal data through your account settings.

green.title: Account deletion available
green.plain_english: You can delete your Dropbox account and your data will be removed within 30 days.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Dropbox does not need your camera or microphone. It only stores files you choose to upload.
categories.detail: No camera or microphone access required.

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Dropbox does not track your location. It only cares about your files, not where you are.
categories.detail: No location collection mentioned in the policy.

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: Dropbox can access your contacts if you choose to share files with people from your address book. Your contacts are uploaded to Dropbox's servers.
categories.detail: Contacts accessed for sharing files with others. Uploaded to servers.
concerns: Contacts uploaded to servers for sharing

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Dropbox needs access to your files so it can store and sync them. This is the main purpose of the app. Your files are encrypted.
categories.detail: Full file access is required for cloud storage and syncing. Files are encrypted at rest.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Dropbox shares some data with trusted companies that help provide the service, but it does not sell your data to advertisers.
categories.detail: Shared with trusted third parties for support, corporate affiliates, collaborators, and API-connected apps.
categories.policy_excerpt: Dropbox will not sell data to advertisers. It shares information with trusted third parties handling support duties, other firms within the Dropbox corporate group, and fellow collaborators. Third-party applications linked through APIs exchange data governed by their own terms.
concerns: API-connected apps have their own data rules

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: Dropbox needs your email and phone number to create an account. This is standard for cloud storage services.
categories.detail: Account information like emails and phone numbers collected for account management.
categories.policy_excerpt: account information like emails and phone numbers

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Dropbox does not track your behavior to show you ads. They don't sell your data to advertisers at all.
categories.detail: No behavioral tracking or ad targeting. Cookies used only for service functionality.
categories.policy_excerpt: Dropbox will not sell data to advertisers. Cookies and similar technologies track interactions for service functionality and promotions.

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The policy doesn't say anything specific about how Dropbox handles children's data.
categories.detail: No specific children's data handling information found.

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Dropbox logs your internet activity to keep the service running and secure. This is normal for cloud storage.
categories.detail: Usage activity logged for service functionality and security.

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Dropbox collects device identifiers to recognize your devices and keep your account secure.
categories.detail: Device identifiers collected for security and service functionality.

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: Dropbox does not collect health or biometric data.
categories.detail: No health or biometric data collection.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: Dropbox does not handle payments in the app. Upgrades are done through the App Store.
categories.detail: No payment data collection in the app.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete your Dropbox account and your data, but it takes 30 days and some copies might stay on backups longer.
categories.detail: Users may access, amend, download, and delete personal data. Following account deletion, Dropbox initiates deletion after 30 days, though residual copies may persist briefly on backups or longer where legal obligations demand.
categories.policy_excerpt: Users may access, amend, download, and delete personal data through account settings. Following account deletion, Dropbox will initiate deletion of this information after 30 days, though residual copies may persist briefly on backups or longer where legal obligations demand.

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: The policy doesn't clearly say how Dropbox will tell you if the rules change.
categories.detail: No specific policy change notification mechanism mentioned.
